pr_title: net: coap: Fix response matching algorithm
pr_body:
* Add test case for matching pending replies with received responses.
Cover corner cases that are failing with the current implementation.

* Fix response matching algorithm 

Fixes #84100
pr_comments: @boaks Thanks for the detailed review, please revisit.

Changes in latest push:
* Added/updated a few more test cases (mostly for the RST case)
* Added special handling for RST packets, so that they are still forwarded to the application callback but **only** if MID matches
* Added extra commit with coap_packet_is_request() function fix - the function wrongly interpreted empty code as a request

> @Aluleichtbau Thanks for the test cases, I've extended the test list in this PR and I think we're pretty much covered now. Two caveats though:
> 
>     * a few of your test cases wrongly assumed that for a separate response MID has to match,
> 
>     * I've skipped tests for NON CON, IMO they're redundant as from reply matching perspective there's not really a difference between CON and NON CON, both are treated as separate replies

You are right. There was still an issue with them, I updated them. NON_CON and CON is indeed equal. I copied them just for sake of completeness, but removing NON_CON is also fine. Thank you!
I see they've merged some Clang-related hotfix yesterday evening, let's try a rerun.

issue_context.title: net: coap: Request/Response Matching Rules (RFC 7252 section-5.3.2) are not applied correctly
issue_context.body:
<!--
**Notes**
Github Discussions (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/discussions)
are available to first verify that the issue is a genuine Zephyr bug and not a
consequence of Zephyr services misuse.

This issue list is only for bugs in the main Zephyr code base
(https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/). If the bug is for a project
fork (such as NCS) specific feature, please open an issue in the fork project
instead.
-->

**Describe the bug**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - What target platform are you using?
 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?
 - Is this a regression? If yes, have you been able to "git bisect" it to a
   specific commit?
 - ...
-->

`coap_response_received` function is used to find (and handle) a received response in an array of expected `struct coap_reply`. RFC 7252 section-5.3.2 specifies the rules for matching the reply. zTesting my own CoAP client application I stumbled over issues:
- piggybacked ACK with mid not identical are matched anyway if the token matches.
- if the tokenlen in the received message is zero, it still can be matched to replies having a token if they have the same mid

I also wondered why `((r->id == 0U) && (r->tkl == 0U))` is a criterion to not match. In `coap_reply_next_unused` replies are freed if `r->reply == NULL` what might be the purpose of the check.


**To Reproduce**
<!--
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. mkdir build; cd build
2. cmake -DBOARD=board\_xyz
3. make
4. See error
-->

0. Make sure you have a callback
```c
static int response_handled_cb(const struct coap_packet *response,
			     struct coap_reply *reply,
			     const struct sockaddr *from)
{
	return 0;
}
```
1. Create a reply array like this:
```c
	struct coap_reply replies[] = {
		{.id = 124, .token = "token", .tkl = 5, .reply = response_handled_cb},
		{.id = 125, .token = "other", .tkl = 5, .reply = response_handled_cb},
	};
```
3. Create a coap_packet like this:
```c
	struct coap_packet response = {0};
	coap_packet_init(&response, data, COAP_BUF_SIZE, COAP_VERSION_1, COAP_TYPE_ACK,
			     strlen("other"), "other", COAP_RESPONSE_CODE_CONTENT, 124);
```
4. Call `coap_response_received(&response, &from, &replies[0], ARRAY_SIZE(replies))` and you will get the 2nd element from the list.
5. Create another coap_packet like this:
```c
	coap_packet_init(&response, data, COAP_BUF_SIZE, COAP_VERSION_1, COAP_TYPE_CON,
			     0, NULL, COAP_RESPONSE_CODE_CONTENT, 124);
```
6. Call `coap_response_received(&response, &from, &replies[0], ARRAY_SIZE(replies))` and you will get the  1st element of the list.

**Expected behavior**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
-->
RFC says:
> In a piggybacked response, the Message ID of the Confirmable request and the Acknowledgement MUST match, and the tokens of the response and original request MUST match. In a separate response, just the tokens of the response and original request MUST match.

So in 4. and 6. nothing shall be called and NULL shall be returned.

**Impact**
<!--
What impact does this issue have on your progress (e.g., annoyance, showstopper)
-->
coap implementation is not compliant to RFC 7252 section-5.3.2.

**Logs and console output**
<!--
If applicable, add console logs or other types of debug information
e.g Wireshark capture or Logic analyzer capture (upload in zip archive).
copy-and-paste text and put a code fence (\`\`\`) before and after, to help
explain the issue. (if unable to obtain text log, add a screenshot)
-->
N/A

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: Windows 10, WSL Ubuntu
 - Toolchain Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA: 4e201f21c8a7f58698e68a5f1cca72433f9778ac

**Additional context**
<!--
Add any other context that could be relevant to your issue, such as pin setting,
target configuration, ...
-->
I prepared tests and fixes for this, I will provide soon.
comments:
> if the tokenlen in the received message is zero, it still can be matched to replies having a token if they have the same mid

Not sure, what this means exactly. If the request uses an empty token, only a response with empty tokens will match. 

[RFC 7252 5.3.1 Token](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7252#section-5.3.1)

> The client SHOULD generate tokens in such a way that tokens currently
> in use for a given source/destination endpoint pair are unique.
> ...
> An empty token value is appropriate e.g., when
> no other tokens are in use to a destination, or when requests are
> made serially per destination and receive piggybacked responses.

RFC 7252 5.3.2 also applies, so a request with an empty token is matched by a response with an empty token. If it's a piggybacked response (ACK), then also the MID must match.

> RFC 7252 5.3.2 also applies, so a request with an empty token is matched by a response with an empty token. If it's a piggybacked response (ACK), then also the MID must match.

If I understood correctly, in the described bug only the response had an empty token. The request carried a non-empty token, yet still the response with no token is matched.

I'll look into this.
I left some comments on the PR.

I just realized that the function is not used on every received response. `subsys/net/lib/coap/coap_client.c` does not use the function at all, `zephyr/samples/net/sockets/coap_client/src/coap-client.c` uses it to `process_obs_coap_reply`, and `zephyr/subsys/net/lib/lwm2m/lwm2m_message_handling.c` uses it generally (see `lwm2m_udp_receive`), but does not call it if it is an empty ACK on an existing `pending`. But when it comes to observables, there might be no pending. But what is the meaning of an empty ACK on an observable? Empty ACK addresses pendings and are no real response to be handled by the function `coap_response_received`. They should be ignored by the function generally. So that is an issue with the tests by me above - need to update them.

However, empty RESET shall be handled.

@Aluleichtbau Please comment on https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/84160, there's some ongoing discussion in there already. 

> However, empty RESET shall be handled.

@boaks The RESET message bugs me, sure according to the table mentioned in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/84160#discussion_r1920530374 RESET is not a valid reply, but still in other parts of the RFC (like https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7252#page-11):

> When a recipient is not at all able to process a Confirmable message (i.e., not even able to provide a suitable error response), it
   replies with a Reset message (RST) instead of an Acknowledgement (ACK).

> When a recipient is not able to process a Non-confirmable message, it may reply with a Reset message (RST).

So perhaps we should still try to match RESET replies with MID only and call the registered callback? Otherwise the client has no notion that the request was rejected.

> o perhaps we should still try to match RESET replies with MID only and call the registered callback? Otherwise the client has no notion that the request was rejected.

That's right. My statement in the PR was focused on a RESET and the `piggybacked`. 

Beside of the reject, also (in rare cases) a timeout my be relevant for the client to know. 
(I use the coap message encoding /decoding and my own retransmission/matching functions. Therefore I'm not common, how that is handled in zephyr.)

@boaks Timeout-handling on `coap_pending`s is also done by LWM2M in `/subsys/net/lib/lwm2m/lwm2m_engine.c:390`, i.e. outside of the functions of coap.c. However, LWM2M does not seem to transmit or process RESET at all (not sure wheather it actually requires to or not).

`subsys/net/lib/coap/coap_client.c` processes incoming responses in `handle_response` and does not use the `coap_response_received`. It implements RESET, but I am not sure if the matching there is better. There are probably also issues with the matching, e.g. for piggybacked messages token seems to be checked, but id is not.

@boaks Yeah, RFC says the token shall match in that case. But if there is no token and the ID is not checked, the response literally matches to any request without a token. But as far as I read the section 5.3.1 that's the way and you are right. Thanks for the remarks. So I need to update the tests also.

@Aluleichtbau 

> So I need to update the tests also.

Great.

> But if there is no token

[RFC 7252 5.3.1 Token](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7252#section-5.3.1)

>    The Token is used to match a response with a request.  The token
>    value is a sequence of 0 to 8 bytes.  (Note that every message
>    carries a token, even if it is of zero length.)

There is just no **no token**, that's the empty token. 

>  the response literally matches to any request without a token

Again, not "without a token", but with the empty token.

>    The client SHOULD generate tokens in such a way that tokens currently
>    in use for a given source/destination endpoint pair are unique.
>    (Note that a client implementation can use the same token for any
>    request if it uses a different endpoint each time, e.g., a different
>    source port number.)  An empty token value is appropriate e.g., when
>    no other tokens are in use to a destination, or when requests are
>    made serially per destination and receive piggybacked responses.
>    There are, however, multiple possible implementation strategies to
>    fulfill this.

It the same rule for the empty token as for all others: if in use, it must be unique. Otherwise you will mix up the communication.

> Timeout-handling on coap_pendings is also done by LWM2M 

Let me recommend to have that in CoAP as well. Not everybody wants to use CoAP only with LwM2M.

review_comments: Maybe too picky, but RFC 7252 named that "empty token" not "no token". In the case of an empty message (code 0.0) the it may be considered as "no token", but for non empty messages the wording is an empty token.

There is a "ping/pong" definition in RFC 7252 (CON 0.0 => RST 0.0), where, depending on the implementation, an empty CON message may be considered to be a request. 
Not sure, if that is related, but that change may fail with a ping/pong.

I was tempted to change this initially, but TBH after digging into RFC 7252 I'm not sure if we should consider such an empty CON "probe" as a request. Specifically, chapter 4.1 defines an empty message separately from request/response:
> Separate from the message type, a message may carry a request, a response, or be Empty.

Similarily in chapter 4.2 an empty message is considered separately from regular request/response:
> A Confirmable message always carries either a request or response, unless it is used only to elicit a Reset message, in which case it is Empty.

Of course if the above assumption is not a valid one I guess we could just add an extra type check to the function instead.

The one view is the wording, and with that the change is well.
The other view is the processing of such an CON 0.0.
I'm not sure, what the logic inside the zephyr functions for that ping/pong is. I'm still on NCS 2.6.2 so I don't see the current implementation (I would need to check that out to see, how such a ping pong is intended to be processed. I will go for that tomorrow.) 

Edited:
I checked out the PR.
`coap_packet_is_request` is mainly used for blockwise transfer to distinguish from block1 and block2.
I can't see it's used to detect somewhere a "ping".
So the change is well.

A RST is always a empty message and no piggybacked response.

See [RFC 7252, page 23, table 1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7252#page-23)

```
+----------+-----+-----+-----+-----+
|          | CON | NON | ACK | RST |
+----------+-----+-----+-----+-----+
| Request  | X   | X   | -   | -   |
| Response | X   | X   | X   | -   |
| Empty    | *   | -   | X   | X   |
+----------+-----+-----+-----+-----+
  Table 1: Usage of Message Types
```
